passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Results of Operations The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and the related notes thereto included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. In addition to historical financial information, the following discussion and analysis contains forward-looking statements that involve risks, uncertainties, and assumptions as described under the “Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements” that appears earlier in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Our actual results could differ materially from those anticipated by these forward-looking statements as a result of many factors, including those discussed under Item 1A. “Risk Factors,” and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. This discussion and analysis does not address certain items in respect of the year ended December 31, 2023. See Item 7. “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 for comparative discussions of our results of operations and liquidity and capital resources for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023. Executive Overview We are America’s leading PV solar technology and manufacturing company. The only U.S.-headquartered company among the world’s largest solar manufacturers, First Solar is focused on competitively and reliably enabling power generation needs with our advanced, uniquely American thin film PV technology. Developed at R&D labs in California and Ohio, our technology provides a competitive, high-performance, and responsibly produced alternative to conventional crystalline silicon PV solar modules. Our PV solar modules are produced using a fully integrated, continuous process that does not rely on Chinese crystalline silicon supply chains. We are the world’s largest thin film PV solar module manufacturer and the largest PV solar module manufacturer in the Western Hemisphere. We recently commenced operations at our fourth and fifth manufacturing facilities in the United States and completed the expansion of our manufacturing footprint at our existing facilities in Ohio. We are in the process of further expanding our domestic manufacturing capacity, including the construction of our sixth U.S. manufacturing facility to onshore final production processes for modules initiated by our international fleet, which is expected to commence operations in the second half of 2026. Our global manufacturing footprint spans the United States, India, Malaysia, and Vietnam. Certain of our financial results and other key operational developments for the year ended December 31, 2025 include the following: • Net sales for 2025 increased by 24% to $5.2 billion compared to $4.2 billion in 2024. The increase in net sales was primarily driven by an increase in the volume of modules sold to third parties. 51 Table of Contents • Gross profit as a percentage of net sales decreased 3.6 percentage points to 40.6% in 2025 from 44.2% in 2024. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: An investment in our stock involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the following information, together with the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, before buying shares of our stock. If any of the following risks or uncertainties occur, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be materially and adversely affected and the trading price of our stock could decline. Summary of Risk Factors The following is a summary of the principal risks and uncertainties that could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations and make an investment in our stock speculative or risky. You should read this summary together with the more detailed description of each risk factor contained below. Risks Related to Our Markets and Customers • Competition in solar markets globally and across the solar value chain is intense and could remain that way for an extended period of time. The solar industry may experience periods of structural imbalance between global PV module supply and demand that result in periods of pricing volatility. If our competitors maintain module pricing at levels near or below their manufacturing costs, or are able to operate at minimal or negative operating margins for sustained periods of time, or if global demand for PV modules decreases relative to installed production capacity, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected. • The modification, reduction, elimination, or expiration of government subsidies, economic incentives, tax incentives, renewable energy targets, and other support for on-grid solar electricity applications, or the impact of other public policies, such as tariffs or other trade remedies imposed on solar cells and modules or related raw materials or equipment, have, and in the future could, negatively impact demand and/or price levels for our solar modules and limit our growth or lead to a reduction in our net sales or increase our costs, thereby adversely impacting our operating results. • The loss of any of our large customers, or the inability of our customers and counterparties to perform under their contracts with us, including through terminations by customers of any contract in part or in full, has reduced and, in the future, could significantly reduce our net sales and negatively impact our results of operations. credit_strengths.text: First Solar's revenue and operating income have grown steadily across the last three fiscal years, with operating margin well above the sector median. This reflects strong demand for its thin-film modules and a differentiated domestic manufacturing footprint. The resulting earnings base provides a substantial cushion for fixed charges and supports internal cash generation.

The company maintains a net cash position, with cash and short-term investments exceeding total debt. Gross leverage is minimal and net leverage is negative, placing it in the strongest tier of the indicative financial risk profile. Liquidity is further supported by a current ratio comfortably above the sector median.

key_risks.text: The debt note shows the India Credit Facility is the largest borrowing, with a current portion due within the next twelve months. While the overall debt burden is small, refinancing or repayment of this facility depends on continued access to local bank lines and could absorb liquidity if Indian operations underperform.

Risk factors highlight intense competition and potential structural imbalance between global module supply and demand, which could pressure pricing and margins. Additionally, reliance on government subsidies and tariffs means adverse policy changes could reduce demand or increase costs, directly affecting cash flow generation.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is exceptionally high, far exceeding the sector median, and operating cash flow covers total debt multiple times over. Free cash flow after capital expenditures also remains substantial relative to debt, indicating ample capacity to service obligations from internal resources without relying on external financing.

The maturity profile is well laddered, with the next twelve months representing only a modest portion of total debt and no single year exceeding a manageable amount. This reduces refinancing risk. However, the India Credit Facility is the dominant component, so repayment depends on the performance of Indian operations and local banking conditions.

overall_credit_view.text: First Solar presents a minimal credit risk profile, underpinned by net cash, high margins, and robust cash flow. Leverage is far below the sector median and interest coverage is exceptionally strong. The company's differentiated technology and domestic manufacturing footprint support a stable earnings outlook, though policy and competitive risks warrant monitoring.

Analyst judgement: the company is well positioned to withstand sector cyclicality given its net cash position and substantial free cash flow. However, the concentration of debt in the India Credit Facility and exposure to subsidy and trade policy changes are key sensitivities. Continued capacity expansion may absorb cash, but current liquidity provides a strong buffer.

credit_strengths.text: First Solar 於過去三個財政年度的收入及經營溢利均穩步增長，經營利潤率遠高於行業中位數。這反映其薄膜組件需求強勁，以及其具差異化的本土製造佈局。由此產生的盈利基礎為固定費用提供充裕緩衝，並支持內部現金生成。
公司維持淨現金狀況，現金及短期投資超過總債務。總槓桿極低，淨槓桿為負，使其處於指示性財務風險狀況中最強一級。流動性進一步受惠於流動比率穩居行業中位數之上。

key_risks.text: 債務附註顯示，India Credit Facility 為最大借款，其中流動部分將於未來十二個月內到期。儘管整體債務負擔較小，該融資的再融資或償付取決於能否持續獲得當地銀行額度，若印度業務表現欠佳，可能吸納流動性。
風險因素凸顯激烈競爭，以及全球組件供需可能出現結構性失衡，或對定價及利潤率構成壓力。此外，依賴政府補貼及關稅意味不利政策變動可能減少需求或增加成本，直接影響現金流生成。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率異常高，遠超行業中位數，而經營現金流覆蓋總債務多倍。扣除資本開支後的自由現金流相對於債務亦仍然可觀，顯示有充裕能力以內部資源償付債務，而無需依賴外部融資。
到期結構分佈良好，未來十二個月僅佔總債務一小部分，且並無任何單一年份超過可控金額。這降低再融資風險。然而，India Credit Facility 為主要組成部分，故償付取決於印度業務表現及當地銀行狀況。

overall_credit_view.text: First Solar 呈現極低信貸風險狀況，受淨現金、高利潤率及強勁現金流支撐。槓桿遠低於行業中位數，利息覆蓋率異常強勁。公司具差異化的技術及本土製造佈局支持穩定盈利前景，惟政策及競爭風險值得監察。
分析師判斷：鑑於其淨現金狀況及可觀自由現金流，公司具良好條件抵禦行業週期性。然而，債務集中於 India Credit Facility，以及對補貼及貿易政策變動的敞口，為主要敏感因素。持續產能擴張可能吸納現金，但當前流動性提供強大緩衝。
